qwen3_direct_tailoring_results.independent_structural_finding: A direct probe (title_inflation_probe.json) shows that even a HYPOTHETICAL perfect/clean local realization would still fail validation for 3 of the 4 jobs (27323, 7267, 7406), because merge_realization() copies the job posting's raw title verbatim into the resume header with no grounding check, and validate_json_fields' title-inflation guard (decision #62) then rejects any elevated word ('engineer') not present in this candidate's authoritative titles. This means the 0% success rate above is not just a qwen3 quality problem -- it is at least partly a model-agnostic architecture gap in degraded mode. See title_inflation_probe.json for the isolated repro.

comparison_to_cloud_baseline.note: No cloud LLM call was made in this experiment for a fresh comparison (cloud providers were in fact live-attempted by request_local_realization's fallback chain and hit real daily quota limits before falling through to local -- see run.log). Comparison instead uses pre-existing, real cloud-tailored artifacts already on disk.

0/4 real jobs produced usable output in this sample -- 2 malformed JSON, 1 fully safety-rejected, 1 correctly gated before the model ran. ~62s/job latency for zero yield. A structural title-grounding gap in merge_realization() means even a hypothetically perfect local model would still fail 3 of these 4 jobs today.

Cloud-tailored baselines for the same jobs addressed 7-8/8 requirements each vs. 0/8 for local-only in this sample. This matches the original Q2 A/B conclusion (local planning provided no coverage improvement and was 2x slower) and extends it: local-only DIRECT tailoring (no cloud involvement at all) is materially worse, not just neutral.

answer_to_core_question: No. No genuinely small resume-tailoring-specialized model was runnable in this environment to test directly (all 4 named candidates verified as either non-runnable without new infrastructure, non-existent, or impractically large for this hardware). The only runnable local model, qwen3:1.7b (a GENERIC model, not resume-specialized), produced zero usable tailored output across 4 real jobs with materially different characteristics -- worse than the already-unfavorable Q2 finding for it as a planning-signal model. The existing deterministic-extraction + cloud-realization architecture remains the only path in this system that reliably produces validated, truthful, requirement-covering tailored resumes; nothing tested here challenges that.
